newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai Airways to lease, not buy planes.
newsitem.headline: Thai Airways to lease, not buy planes.

text.p: Thai Airways International Plc said on Thursday it would switch from buying to leasing six Boeing aircraft that it is due take delivery of this year.

Thai Airways president Thamnoon Wanglee told reporters the decision was partly in response to a government request for the carrier to consider trimming its foreign exchange spending while Thailand seeks to narrow its wide current account deficit.
Thai Airways chairman Mahidol Chantrangkul said the planes to be leased were not part of a separate 21-aircraft expansion plan for the 1996-2000 period.

He said the carrier, 93 percent owned by the government, would consult the finance ministry on what financing arrangement should be made on the second group of 21 planes that Thai Aircraft earlier intended to buy.
Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan has said Thai Airways should lease the 21 aircraft.
Thamnoon said the six planes being leased included two Boeing 747-400s and four Boeing 777-200s due for delivery between April and December this year.
He said the aircraft were part of 12 planes that the government had allowed Thai Airways to buy since 1992.
"I don't expect any problems (from Boeing) in switching from buying to leasing these planes," he said.
